title: Solver sensitivity: for which solver do text skills matter? Pilot on 98 SearchQA training items: glm-5.3-flash vs glm-5.3 vs deepseek-v4-flash with thinking off (cal-1), plus a re-analysis of the 10/15 probe and a format diagnostic
purpose: Serves purpose 2 (generalisation as the metric, "刷分": a measurable, honest score change when a Skill evolved on one benchmark is evaluated) by choosing the solver and measurement setup in which skill text has a detectable, rule-specific effect. It also serves purpose 1 (co-evolution) indirectly: the verifier side can only learn from what the solver's scores actually measure, and on deepseek with thinking off they are dominated by an answer-format artifact.
verdict_cn:
一句话结论：换求解模型（求解模型＝真正答题的那个大模型），确实能让“文字技能”的效果看得见，三个里最好的是 glm-5.3-flash（开思考）。但换模型不能让“学到的规则胜过写好的任务说明”成立。更要紧的发现是：v3 用的 deepseek（不思考）上“规则没用”，很大一部分是答案格式问题，不是内容问题。修好评分就能看见规则的效果，这一步不花钱，应该先做。

做了什么：
- 题目：从 cal-1 同一批 200 道 SearchQA 训练题里随机抽 100 道。其中 2 道被智谱接口的内容安全过滤拒答，实际比较 98 道。
- 提示词：与 cal-1 逐字节相同。
- 三个求解模型：
  - deepseek-v4-flash 不思考：直接用 cal-1 已有的每题 4 次结果。
  - glm-5.3-flash 开思考：新跑，每题每种文字 2 次。
  - glm-5.3 开思考、低强度：新跑，每题每种文字 2 次。实际只有约 13% 的题真的思考了。
- 四种文字：
  - 空骨架：只有五个标题。
  - 手写任务卡：五段任务说明。
  - v3 学到的一条规则：“只答最短的名字或短语”。
  - 一段无关文字：讲菜谱格式，作“安慰剂”。只在 flash 上跑了 1 次。
- 花费：约 287 万 token（token 是计费的字数单位），上限 300 万。

结果（“点”＝每 100 题多对几题；“好/差”＝变好/变差的题数）：
1. 手写任务卡 比 空骨架，三个模型都明显受益：
   - flash：多 14.3 点（22 好 1 差）；
   - deepseek：多 10.2 点（19 好 4 差）；
   - glm-5.3：多 9.2 点（14 好 1 差）。
2. 学到的那一条规则 比 空骨架：
   - flash：多 13.8 点（21 好 2 差），两次重跑各自都显著，和整张任务卡一样大；
   - glm-5.3：多 6.1 点，不显著；
   - deepseek：少 4.6 点，不显著。
3. 无关文字（安慰剂）：flash 上为 0（8 好 8 差），所以 flash 的提升是规则内容本身带来的；deepseek 上少 9.2 点。
4. 学到的规则 比 手写任务卡：flash 少 0.5 点（4 好 4 差），glm-5.3 少 3.1 点，deepseek 更差。没有一个模型上规则胜过好的任务说明。
5. deepseek 为什么看不出：
   - 加了规则或无关文字后，它常常不用要求的 <answer> 答案标签，改用 JSON（一种数据格式）回答，例如 {"answer": "U2"}，现有评分器读不出就判错。
   - 加那条规则时，只有 61% 的回答带标签；任务卡下是 99.9%。只要回答带标签，各种文字下的正确率几乎一样（71%–78%）。
   - 如果评分器也读 JSON 答案（这是我做的诊断性重算，不是登记的评分器），在 cal-1 的 200 题、每题 4 次上：那条规则从少 2.6 点变成多 6.75 点（可信区间 3.0 到 10.6 点）；无关文字从少 9.8 点变成少 0.25 点。
   - 可见 v3 在 SearchQA 上“规则通不过”，很大程度是格式造成的。两个 GLM 模型几乎 100% 都用标签，没有这个问题。
6. flash 上的提升，具体是去掉答案里多余的括号说明，例如 “Brutus (Marcus Junius Brutus)” 变成 “Brutus”。这是答案写法上的改进，不是知识增加。

文献怎么说：没有“越弱的模型越吃提示”的一致规律。
- SkillsBench（2026）：人工写的技能让 7 个模型配置都提高 13.6 到 23.3 点，最强的模型提高最多。
- Dynamic Cheatsheet（2025）：小模型和推理模型几乎不提高。
- DeepSeek-R1 论文自己写着：它对提示很敏感。
- 关键是三件事：模型本身能不能做这类题；它犯的错是不是文字能改的；输出格式稳不稳。

建议：
① 先在 v4 修答案格式，不花钱，对任何模型都有用。做法是让评分器认 JSON 答案，或者把“答案写在 <answer> 里”这句放到提示最后。然后用新评分重新计算 cal-1 和 v3 的 SearchQA 门槛结果（门槛＝接受规则前的检验）。
② 为“刷分”加一条事先登记的 glm-5.3-flash 求解方案：
   - 它效果最大、安慰剂无效、标签 100%、同一文字重跑结果翻转少（4% 到 9%）。
   - 要检测一条规则这么大的效果，大约 50 道题就够；deepseek 修好格式后约需 120 到 140 道。
   - 先跑“cal-1 的 flash 版”：约 1500 万 token，约 80 分钟。
   - 再在 OfficeQA（文档问答）真题上测迁移：约 1000 万 token，4 到 5 小时；同时用修好格式的 deepseek 复核：约 500 万 token。
③ 风险：
   - flash 和负责出题、诊断、写规则的 GLM-5.3 是同一家族。以前见过“生成题上的提升只在 GLM 家族里出现，换 deepseek 就消失”，所以迁移效果必须用真题测，并用 deepseek 做跨家族复核。
   - flash 在 OfficeQA 上很慢、常被截断：真题每题约 1.7 万 token，19% 超过 3.2 万 token 的上限，平均 159 秒一题。
   - 不要用 GLM-5.3 本身做求解模型，因为它就是方法里所有角色的模型。
④ 任务里的第 (c) 项（deepseek 开思考）没能跑：
   - PJLAB 通道的白名单规定只能关思考；另一条允许的免费通道现在配额用完（报错 403）。
   - 10/15 的旧数据里，deepseek 开思考时 100% 用标签，任务说明的效果和 GLM 相近，学到的规则比任务说明仍约为 0。
   - 还有一个想区分原因的小实验没跑成：格式问题到底是因为“不思考”，还是因为 v3 把答案要求挪到了提示前面（约 9 万 token）。两台机器都被 deepseek 的“每分钟请求数上限”挡住（报错 429），命令已备好。
what_i_did:
1. Read both context files and the cal-1 registration (now complete: 8,800 cells; analysis run at 23:43). Read `scripts/weak_solver_probe.py` MODELS/ROUTES:
   - glm-5.3: thinking enabled, effort low.
   - glm-5.3-flash: thinking enabled.
   - deepseek-v4-flash: free_router with thinking unspecified, or the pjlab_token route, which fixes thinking to "disabled".
   - Nothing was added to any allow-list.
2. Audited an earlier, interrupted E7 attempt (19:17-19:24). Its 100-item set was not the cal-1 set (wrong loader), so I rebuilt everything in fresh `run2/` folders.
3. Rebuilt the 200 cal-1 items with the registered loader (frozen v3 snapshot, DATA_SEED 20261017; training pool only, the loader refuses test ids), asserted equality with cal-1's item set, and drew a seeded 100-item subset (65 historical-train, 35 historical-val items).
4. Exported all 8,800 cal-1 cells read-only and reproduced the registered A3/A5 numbers exactly. Re-scored every stored response on the pilot items with the frozen scorer: all verdicts agree (2,987 pass, 1,406 fail).
5. Dry run: all 900 requests (9 arms x 100 items) are byte-identical to cal-1's. The solver and scorer code is md5-identical between /data/skillopt-work and the frozen snapshot.
6. Smokes (24 cells per model), then the main runs on the new machine (3 workers each): parent:A, ids-full and cand x 100 items x 2 runs for glm-5.3-flash and glm-5.3 (600 cells each). Then a placebo add-on: control:3 x 100 x 1 run on glm-5.3-flash. Then one max_tokens=65536 acceptance call.
7. Analyses:
   - paired item-level deltas (bootstrap, t and sign tests), per run index;
   - run-to-run flips; power (items for 80% power) and minimum detectable effects;
   - cross-solver correlation of per-item effects;
   - answer-tag use and failure typing (no tag / near miss / wrong);
   - what the task card fixes, and what remains under it.
8. Diagnostic (no model calls): re-scored all 8,800 cal-1 cells with a JSON-aware answer extraction.
9. Re-analysed the 10/15-16 solver-strength probe read-only:
   - 8 directories: GLM-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, deepseek through the free router (thinking on in 100% of cells), glm-4-flash-250414;
   - benchmarks and items: OfficeQA real and generated items, SearchQA generated items;
   - quantities: instruction and learned effects, reasoning shares, tag use, truncation, latency and flips.
10. Prepared a deepseek historical-layout probe to separate prompt layout from thinking mode. It was blocked by HTTP 429 (RPM limit) on the first cell from both machines; 0 tokens charged.
11. Literature survey with primary sources checked (the DeepSeek-R1 passage verified verbatim in the PDF).
12. The final report file could not be written: the harness refused (`Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files`). The full report is in this structured output.
evidence:
ALL MEASURED unless marked. Setup: 98 common SearchQA training items (100 drawn; 2 refused by BigModel's content filter, HTTP 400 code 1301, for every arm and run, and excluded for every solver). Runs 0-1 unless noted. Registered scorer. "Paired" = per-item pass share, item bootstrap CI (4,000 draws), up/down/tie in items, two-sided sign test p.

A. Pass rates: parent:A | ids-full | cand | control:3
- deepseek-v4-flash, thinking off (cal-1): 0.674 | 0.776 | 0.628 | 0.582
- glm-5.3-flash, thinking on: 0.679 | 0.821 | 0.816 | 0.673 (1 run)
- glm-5.3, thinking enabled, effort low: 0.704 | 0.796 | 0.765 | not run
- Reasoning actually used by glm-5.3: 79/588 answered cells (13.4%).

B. Paired effects (mean [95% CI], up/down/tie, p)
- deepseek, thinking off:
  - ids-full - parent: +0.102 [+0.036, +0.174], 19/4/75, p=0.003
  - cand - parent: -0.046 [-0.133, +0.041], 13/17/68, p=0.58
  - control:3 - parent: -0.092 [-0.158, -0.031], 7/21/70, p=0.013
  - parent:B - parent (same text): 0.000 [-0.046, +0.046], 8/8
  - cand - ids-full: -0.148, 5/24
  - with all 4 runs: ids-full +0.112 [0.051, 0.176] 26/5; cand -0.033 17/20; control:3 -0.079 8/27
  - registered cal-1, 200 items x 4 runs: ids-full +0.0938 [0.051, 0.137] 48/13/139; cand -0.026 37/44; parent:B +0.0075 22/18; control:3 -0.0975 16/58
- glm-5.3-flash:
  - ids-full - parent: +0.143 [+0.082, +0.209], 22/1/75, p<1e-4
  - cand - parent: +0.138 [+0.071, +0.204], 21/2/75, p=0.0001
  - control:3 (1 run) - parent: -0.005 [-0.066, +0.056], 8/8/82 (run 0 vs run 0: 0.000, 6/6)
  - cand - ids-full: -0.005 [-0.041, +0.026], 4/4/90
- glm-5.3:
  - ids-full - parent: +0.092 [+0.041, +0.148], 14/1/83, p=0.001
  - cand - parent: +0.061 [-0.005, +0.133], 14/7/77, p=0.19
  - cand - ids-full: -0.031 [-0.087, +0.020], 5/11

C. Per run index, net items (up/down)
- flash cand: run 0 +14 (15/1), run 1 +13 (15/2). flash ids-full: +16 (17/1), +12 (13/1). flash control:3: 0 (6/6).
- glm-5.3 cand: +9 (11/2), +3 (11/8).
- deepseek cand: -1, -8, -6, +3. deepseek control:3: -1, -17, -6, -7. deepseek ids-full: +14, +6, +11, +13.
- deepseek parent:A pass counts by run on 100 items: 64, 71, 67, 67 (ids-full: 78, 78, 79, 80).

D. Noise: share of items whose run-0 and run-1 verdicts differ
- deepseek: parent 12.2%, ids-full 3.1%, cand 13.3%, control:3 18.4%
- flash: parent 9.2%, ids-full 5.1%, cand 4.1%
- glm-5.3: parent 6.1%, ids-full 6.1%, cand 8.2%

E. Power (normal approximation, 2 runs, 80% power, two-sided 0.05)
- Items needed: flash ids-full 42, flash cand 49; glm-5.3 ids-full 64, glm-5.3 cand 251; deepseek ids-full 90 (63 with 4 runs); deepseek cand none (effect negative).
- Format-fixed deepseek cand (estimated from the diagnostic): 119-143.
- Minimum detectable effect at n=100: 0.07-0.12 for every solver (item heterogeneity, per-item sd 0.26-0.44).

F. Mechanism: answer-tag use (deepseek, 200 items x 4 runs)
- Share of replies carrying <answer>…</answer>:
  - parent:A 0.898, parent:B 0.891
  - ids-full 0.999, seed-only 0.986
  - seed-rule 0.763, seed-rule3 0.655, cand 0.610
  - control:1 0.866, control:2 0.924, control:3 0.769, control:4 0.896
- Pass rate when tagged: 0.714-0.776 for every arm (cand 0.774 = ids-full 0.774). When untagged: 0.0-0.53.
- Untagged replies are mostly JSON such as {"answer": "Medina"}. The registered fallback normalises this to "answer medina", which fails exact match.
- GLM tag use: 98.5-100% under every arm (flash 100% under all four).

G. Failure types (98 items x 2 runs; no tag / near miss / wrong)
- deepseek: parent 18/30/16; cand 47/16/10; control:3 40/29/13
- flash: parent 0/57/6
- glm-5.3: parent 0/46/12
- What ids-full fixes (parent failures on the items it improves): deepseek 13 no-tag + 8 near miss + 6 wrong; flash 33 near miss + 2 wrong; glm-5.3 18 near miss + 5 wrong.
- Flash examples where cand fixes both runs (9 items): "Brutus (Marcus Junius Brutus)" to "Brutus"; "Richmond (Virginia)" to "Richmond"; "Sirius Satellite Radio" to "Sirius".
- Remaining failures under ids-full: 16 (flash) and 18 (glm-5.3), largely the same items. About half are inconsistent gold conventions (gold "Huckabee" vs pred "Mike Huckabee", but gold "Patricia Hearst"; "Forbes magazine"; "Funk & Wagnalls"), the rest wrong answers.

H. JSON-aware re-scoring of 8,800 cal-1 cells (DIAGNOSTIC, not the registered scorer)
- 326 cells flip from fail to pass; none has more than one answer field.
- Paired delta vs parent:A, 200 items x 4 runs, registered then JSON-aware:
  - cand: -0.026 to **+0.0675 [0.030, 0.106]**, 44/19
  - seed-rule3: -0.030 to +0.031 [0.003, 0.061]
  - control:3: -0.0975 to -0.0025 [-0.035, +0.028]
  - ids-full: +0.094 to +0.078 [0.038, 0.121]
  - parent:B: +0.0075 to -0.004
  - control:2: stays +0.036 [0.009, 0.064] (unexplained residual placebo effect)
- On the 98 pilot items: ids-full +0.087, cand +0.071 [0.015, 0.133] (15/5, p=0.04), control:3 -0.010.

I. Cross-solver agreement (Pearson r of per-item ids-full effect, 98 items)
- deepseek vs flash 0.10; deepseek vs glm-5.3 0.10; flash vs glm-5.3 0.38. For cand: 0.06, 0.04 and 0.43.
- Items failing both runs with the empty scaffold: 26, 27 and 26 per solver; 18 shared by all three.

J. 10/15-16 probe re-analysis (different panels and baselines; historical layout)
- Per cell: bzero - empty, then learned - bzero, in pp (up/down).
- deepseek through the free router, thinking on in 100% of cells:
  - SearchQA generated (168): +14.9 (31/1) / -1.8, -1.5
  - OfficeQA real train (47): +19.1 (12/1) / +4.2, +1.0, n.s.
  - OfficeQA generated: +25.6 / +0.8, +4.5
- glm-5.3-flash:
  - SearchQA generated: +12.8 (33/2) / +0.6, +0.6
  - OfficeQA train (41): +31.7 (20/0) / -1.2, -6.1
  - OfficeQA generated: +38.7 / +6.5, +8.5 (p=0.012, 0.004)
- GLM-5.3:
  - SearchQA generated: +11.9 / +0.3, -1.5
  - OfficeQA train: +20.0 (18/5) / -2.0, 0.0
  - OfficeQA generated: +24.6 / +12.9, +11.7 (p=1e-4, 2e-4)
- glm-4-flash-250414:
  - SearchQA generated: +5.1 (n.s.)
  - OfficeQA train: 0.0 (floor 4%)
- Tag use was 100% for deepseek with thinking on; GLM-5.3 0.91-0.99.
- OfficeQA real train, per cell:
  - flash: 17,219 tokens, 76/400 truncated at 32K, 159 s mean (p95 542 s), flips 14.6%
  - deepseek with thinking on: 16,297 tokens, 27/400 truncated, 52 s
  - GLM-5.3: 6,860 tokens, 0 truncated, 28 s, flips 22%
- Learned over instruction on generated items appears only in the GLM family (in-family bias; consistent with the 10/16 ledger).

K. Cost per SearchQA cell (prompt + completion tokens; mean s/cell)
- deepseek, thinking off: 1,338 / 3,850 / 1,478 (parent / ids-full / cand)
- flash: 1,349 / 4,214 / 1,438; 2.6 / 7.0 / 2.7 s; one tail cell took 193 s and 14,011 completion tokens; completion grows from 125 to 454 tokens under ids-full
- glm-5.3: 1,239 / 3,777 / 1,312; 1.5-1.9 s
- Tokenizers agree within 2%.
- The flash API accepted max_tokens 65536 (HTTP 200); generation beyond 32K is not verified.
- No 429 or 5xx on BigModel at 3 workers per model.
design:
Proposed v5 measurement design, in order. Pre-register each step under a new protocol version and output directory; never relabel cal-1 or v3.

1. Format fix (free; v4 scope).
   - Register a format-robust SearchQA answer contract and/or extraction: accept a JSON "answer" field when no tag is present, and/or put the answer contract last (historical layout).
   - Re-analyse cal-1 under it as a declared re-analysis.
   - Re-analyse the v3 SearchQA gate cells under it. Read only s*/train, screen and confirm cells, never s*/evaluation/. Question: would any v3 rule have passed C1/C2?
   - Report tag use per arm as a standing diagnostic.
2. Layout-vs-thinking probe (prepared, blocked by 429).
   - deepseek-v4-flash, thinking disabled, PJLAB route, historical layout, cand arm, 60 items x 1 run, about 90K tokens.
   - Baseline from cal-1 on the same 60 items: cand tag use 0.590, pass 0.649 (239 cells); parent:A tag use 0.896, pass 0.671.
   - If tag use rises to about 1.0, the v3 layout causes the drift; otherwise thinking-off or the route does.
3. cal-1-flash (solver-switch calibration).
   - The same 11 cal-1 arms x 200 SearchQA training items x 4 runs on glm-5.3-flash (thinking on, max_tokens 32768): 8,800 cells.
   - Registered A1-A6 analyses plus tag use, failure types and reasoning share.
   - BigModel 1301 refusals are pre-registered shared exclusions.
   - Decision: adopt flash as the primary purpose-2 solver if the C1 passage of cand and seed-rule3 at n=11 is at least 80% with null (parent:B) passage at most 5% and the placebo controls inside ±3 pp.
4. Transfer probe on REAL OfficeQA training items (similar pair SearchQA to OfficeQA).
   - 74 items (historical train 50 + val 24 = the v3 OfficeQA training pool) x 4 arms x 2 runs with flash at max_tokens 65536. Arms: empty scaffold; task card; task card + a SearchQA-learned answer-form rule; placebo of matched length.
   - Report truncations separately as unknown, never as fail.
   - Replicate with format-fixed deepseek as the cross-family check.
   - Never use generated panels as the transfer evidence while the generator, judge and analyst are GLM-family.
5. Role/solver separation: keep GLM-5.3 out of the solver role.
6. Standing reporting:
   - per-solver tag use, run-to-run flips and same-text floor;
   - placebo spread (at least 2 controls);
   - effects against BOTH the empty scaffold and the task card, the latter being the owner's yardstick.

pilot.result:
MEASURED on 98 SearchQA training items (cal-1 set; 2 of 100 refused by the BigModel content filter, code 1301), runs 0-1, requests byte-identical to cal-1.

Handwritten task card (ids-full) vs empty scaffold:
- glm-5.3-flash (thinking on): +14.3 pp [8.2, 20.9], 22 up / 1 down
- deepseek-v4-flash (thinking off, cal-1): +10.2 [3.6, 17.4], 19/4
- glm-5.3 (effort low; reasoned in 13.4% of cells): +9.2 [4.1, 14.8], 14/1

Learned v3 rule (cand) vs empty scaffold:
- flash: +13.8 [7.1, 20.4], 21/2, significant in each run separately
- glm-5.3: +6.1 (n.s.)
- deepseek: -4.6 (n.s.)

Placebo (recipe text): flash -0.5 (8/8, 1 run); deepseek -9.2 (7/21).

cand vs task card: flash -0.5 (4/4), glm-5.3 -3.1, deepseek -14.8. No solver shows learned > good instruction.

Mechanism on deepseek: extra text makes it answer in JSON instead of the <answer> tag. Tag use: cand 61%, control:3 77%, ids-full 99.9%; pass when tagged 0.71-0.78 for every arm. A JSON-aware diagnostic re-score of 8,800 cal-1 cells turns cand from -2.6 to +6.75 [3.0, 10.6] pp and control:3 from -9.8 to -0.25 pp.

GLM tag use is 98.5-100% under every arm. Run-to-run flips: flash 4-9%, glm-5.3 6-8%, deepseek 3-18%. Items for 80% power on a cand-sized effect: flash 49, glm-5.3 251, format-fixed deepseek about 120-140 (estimated).

risks:
1. Scope: one benchmark (SearchQA) and one learned rule (cand, learned from deepseek's failures). The flash gain is an answer-form effect under strict exact match (it strips parenthetical elaborations). It may not transfer to OfficeQA's numeric answers or LiveMath's options, and transfer was not measured here.
2. Same-family coupling: glm-5.3-flash shares the GLM family with the GLM-5.3 analyst, examiner, generator and forward checker. In the 10/15 probe, learned-over-instruction gains on generated items appeared only within the GLM family and vanished on deepseek. Generated panels cannot carry the transfer evidence if flash is the solver.
3. Flash on OfficeQA: on real train items it used 17.2K tokens per cell, 19% of cells were truncated at 32K, and it took 159 s per cell on average (p95 542 s). max_tokens 65536 was accepted, but generation beyond 32K is unverified, so truncation could bias OfficeQA comparisons.
4. The JSON-aware results are a DIAGNOSTIC, not the registered scorer. Any fix must be registered as a new version, and the registered v3/cal-1 readings stay as they are. One placebo (control:2) keeps an unexplained +3.6 pp under it.
5. Confound: the 10/15 deepseek (100% tag use) differs from cal-1 in thinking mode, route and layout at once. The probe that separates them was blocked (429).
6. Timing: the GLM cells (10/21 ~00:00) and the cal-1 deepseek cells (10/20 16:07-19:56) were not interleaved in time. The flash placebo ran about 10 min after the main arms and has only 1 run (CI ±0.06-0.07). The glm-5.3 placebo was not run (budget).
7. "Thinking on" is not uniform: glm-5.3 at the allow-listed effort 'low' reasoned on only 13.4% of SearchQA cells. The 10/15 free-router 'deepseek-flash' response id is assumed (by that probe's allow-list), not verified, to be the same weights as the PJLAB deepseek-v4-flash.
8. BigModel dependencies: the content filter refused 2% of SearchQA items (code 1301); the deepseek PJLAB key is shared and was RPM-limited at the time of writing.
9. Headroom: even on flash, the residual failures under the task card are about 16-18 per 98 items per run, and about half are inconsistent gold conventions. A solver switch does not create the learned-beats-good-instruction effect the owner's yardstick requires (cand - ids-full ≈ 0 on every solver).

recommendation:
1. Do first, for free: the deepseek-v4-flash thinking-off "rules don't help" result on SearchQA is substantially a format artifact. Register a format-robust answer contract or extraction in v4 (the existing audit item "SearchQA format check vs scorer fallback"), and re-analyse cal-1 and the v3 SearchQA gate cells under it.
   - Under the diagnostic, cand is +6.75 pp [3.0, 10.6] and seed-rule3 +3.1 pp [0.25, 6.1] over the empty scaffold, and the strongest placebo is about 0.
   - Report per-arm answer-tag use as a standing diagnostic.
   - Tell D5 and D8 that cal-1's noise and placebo spread on deepseek is partly this artifact.
2. For purpose 2, adopt glm-5.3-flash (thinking on) as a pre-registered additional solver. Calibrate it first (cal-1-flash, about 15M tokens).
   - It is the best measurement instrument of the three: largest effects, placebo ~0, 100% tag use, fewest flips with guidance, and about 49 items for 80% power on a cand-sized effect.
   - Then run the real-item OfficeQA transfer probe (about 10M tokens).
   - Keep format-fixed deepseek as the cross-family replication solver, because flash shares the GLM family with the method roles.
3. Do not use GLM-5.3 itself as the solver, since it runs every method role.
4. Do not expect a solver switch to deliver "learned rule beats a good instruction". cand minus the task card is about 0 on all solvers, and the residual failures under the task card are about half gold-convention noise.
5. Report every result against both the empty scaffold and the task card.
6. Pursue headroom on top of the task card through benchmarks or failure types not already covered by the card (see D9 and D14), not through the solver.
7. Assignment item (c) (deepseek with thinking on) is not available on allowed routes. Use the 10/15 free-router data: 100% tag use, instruction effect +15/+19 pp, learned over instruction about 0.
